title: Creating Alignment: The Search for Possible Futures
summary: What can speculative fiction bring to the work of AI alignment? An invitation to include the people who have spent their lives imagining possible futures—and the humans who will inhabit them.
question: Who gets to imagine the future?
imageAlt: Artwork accompanying Creating Alignment: The Search for Possible Futures

title: We're Building Gods... Whether We Believe in Them or Not
quote: Who decides which values go into the seed?
summary: An exploration of the philosophical assumptions beneath AI alignment: consciousness, conscience, and the values we embed in what we create. A case for bringing more kinds of thought into the room.
question: What values do we build into intelligence?
imageAlt: Artwork accompanying We're Building Gods... Whether We Believe in Them or Not

title: Estrangement: A Strange Kind of Grief
quote: It finally feels safe to miss her.
summary: A personal reflection on losing a parent after years of estrangement. On the boundaries that make survival possible, the memories we put away, and the love that can finally be felt again.
question: How do we hold love and boundaries together?
imageAlt: Artwork accompanying Estrangement: A Strange Kind of Grief

title: The Future of Education
quote: The machines will distill. The humans must discern.
summary: As AI changes what intelligence can do, what should education cultivate? A proposal for learning rooted in history, values, choices, design, and responsibility—and for helping young people exercise their own agency.
question: What should young people learn in an age of AI?
imageAlt: Artwork accompanying The Future of Education

title: The Future of Labor
quote: What if we optimized economic systems for human flourishing instead?
summary: A different vision of work in the age of intelligence: shared gains from automation, time for civic life, and recognition for care. What might productivity make possible if its benefits returned to people?
question: What is all this productivity for?
imageAlt: Artwork accompanying The Future of Labor

title: Sami: A Eulogy, A Parable
summary: Words in remembrance of my sister, Sami. A story of love, extraordinary resilience, and gratitude that continues to ripple through the lives she touched.
question: What can gratitude carry us through?
imageAlt: Artwork accompanying Sami: A Eulogy, A Parable

title: Proposing a Tricameral Legislature: A Thought Experiment
summary: An experiment in representation beyond geographic boundaries. Could a third legislative chamber reflect shared interests across population density, income, and wealth?
question: What would it mean to feel represented?
imageAlt: Artwork accompanying Proposing a Tricameral Legislature: A Thought Experiment

title: The Reconstitution: The Ten Initial Questions
quote: How do we transform a realpolitik into a clearpolitik?
summary: Ten starting points for reimagining democratic life: power, representation, corporations, advertising, economic value, abundance, rights, justice, legitimacy, and the capacity for a constitution to keep evolving.
question: What would we ask if we could begin again?

title: And The Days Go By… Part II: The Journey Beyond 2020
quote: Every breakdown is an opportunity to break through.
summary: From disruption to a shared vision. The second part follows the relationship between communication, changing worldviews, and the work of making space for a different kind of collective future.
question: How does a breakdown become a beginning?
imageAlt: Artwork accompanying And The Days Go By… Part II: The Journey Beyond 2020

title: And The Days Go By…
quote: We need an articulable shared vision
summary: Written in the upheaval of 2020, this essay traces the evolution of worldviews and asks how people seeing different realities might find a shared way forward.
question: How did we get here—and what comes next?
